title: "They Call Him No. 7" — How Korea Reacted to the Son Heung-min Team Rift
description:
Last week, a lawmaker told South Korea's National Assembly that some national team players reportedly refer to captain Son Heung-min as "No. 7" or "that person" instead of using his name. A Korean news clip about it passed 2.6 million views in under a week. Here's what Korea is saying: the anger, the sympathy, the people blaming the federation, and the voices who think it's time for change.

Chapters
0:00 The claim from parliament
1:05 What actually happened
2:50 "How hard must it have been"
4:20 "It wasn't just my imagination"
5:40 Blaming the federation
6:30 The other side
7:40 What happens next

All comments are translated and paraphrased from public comment sections of Korean news videos (JTBC News, Channel A, 2Billion). Usernames removed. Reports of the conflict are allegations raised in the National Assembly and in Korean media; the players involved have not confirmed them.

#SonHeungmin #KoreanReaction #WhatKoreaSays

scenes.small: Not his name. His shirt number.
say: South Korea's captain just became the country's all-time top scorer.
And according to a claim made in parliament last week, some of his own teammates don't even call him by his name.
They call him number seven.

scenes.label: views on one Korean news clip, in under a week
say: A single Korean news clip about it passed two point six million views in less than a week.
So what are Koreans actually saying?
Today we'll go through the claim itself, the comments with thousands of likes, and the people who see it differently.
And at the end, one comment that sums up how a lot of Korea feels right now.

scenes.title: The claim from parliament
say: First, what actually happened.

scenes.head: Some players reportedly call Son "No. 7" or "that person"
say: On October twenty-first, during the National Assembly's annual audit of the Korea Football Association, a lawmaker raised a claim.
Some players on the national team, the lawmaker said, refer to captain Son Heung-min as number seven, or simply that person, instead of saying his name.

scenes.head: Confirmed players had raised "difficulties" — but says locker room issues stay in the locker room
say: When asked, the federation said it had received reports that players were struggling with problems inside the team.
It did not confirm the nickname itself, and said that what happens in the locker room should be solved in the locker room.

scenes.head: The story spread to Japanese and international media within days
say: Within days, the story had spread beyond Korea.
Japanese outlets reported that the turmoil inside the Korean team would likely continue, and Korean broadcasters ran follow-up segments about how the claim was being covered abroad.
For a player as famous as Son, a story like this was never going to stay local.
To understand why this hit so hard in Korea, you need some context.
On October sixth, against Uzbekistan, Son curled a free kick into the bottom corner in the sixth minute.
It was his fifty-ninth goal for Korea. It broke the national record held by Cha Bum-kun, a name every Korean football fan knows, a record that had stood since the nineteen eighties.
In England, Tottenham's official account congratulated him as a Spurs legend. In Los Angeles, his club LAFC posted a message in Korean.
So for Koreans, the timing felt brutal. The week he made history, the story became about what his own teammates call him.

scenes.head: Reports: three players born in 1996 hinted at quitting the national team
say: Around the same time, Korean media reported that three key players born in nineteen ninety-six, Kim Min-jae, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan, had hinted at leaving the national team.
Korean fans call them the ninety-six line.
None of the three has publicly confirmed any conflict with Son.

rows: Asian Cup: night-before-semifinal clash with younger players, Son hurts a finger
Reports of a team-wide interview boycott that divided the squad
say: And this isn't the first time.

Back in January twenty twenty-four, on the night before the Asian Cup semifinal, Son clashed with younger players who wanted to play table tennis after dinner. He dislocated a finger. Lee Kang-in later flew to London to apologize in person, and Son publicly forgave him.
During this summer's World Cup, Korean outlets reported that the team boycotted interviews after criticism of Son, and that not every player was happy about it.
So when the number seven claim came out, many Koreans didn't see a single incident. They saw a pattern.

scenes.title: "How hard must it have been"
say: Second. The first wave of reactions was not anger. It was sympathy.

scenes.ko: 아 흥민아 그동안 얼마나 힘들었니 마음이 아프다
scenes.en: Oh, Heung-min. How hard must it have been all this time. My heart hurts.
say: Under the JTBC news clip, one of the most liked comments reads:
Oh, Heung-min. How hard must it have been all this time. My heart hurts.

scenes.ko: 손흥민 진짜 보살이다… 겁난다 손흥민 은퇴할까봐
scenes.en: He's honestly a saint. Now I'm scared he'll retire.
say: Another, with over two thousand likes, calls him a saint, a word Koreans use for someone with almost unreal patience.
And then it adds: now I'm scared he'll retire.

scenes.en: No. 7?? Zero respect for a legend.
say: The most common feeling was simple disbelief.
Number seven? Zero respect for a legend. That one has three thousand likes.

scenes.en: Just leave Heung-min alone. He's on a completely different level.
say: Under a pundit interview, a shorter one says it all.
Just leave Heung-min alone. He's on a completely different level.

scenes.ko: 손흥민이 지금까지도 참아온게 더 대단하다고 느껴지네
scenes.en: What amazes me more is that he put up with all of this until now.
say: And a theme that came up again and again: what amazes people is not the claim itself, but that he kept quiet through all of it.
What amazes me more is that he put up with this until now.

scenes.title: "It wasn't just my imagination"
say: Third. This is where it gets interesting.
Many Koreans started looking back at matches they had already watched.

scenes.ko: 손흥민이 국대가면 표정이 어둡고 클럽팀 복귀하면 표정이 밝은게 나만 느낀게 아니었구나
scenes.en: So I wasn't the only one who noticed. He always looked gloomy with the national team and bright at his club.
say: One viewer wrote that Son always seemed gloomy with the national team, and bright again whenever he went back to his club.
So I wasn't the only one who noticed.

scenes.ko: 그동안 패스가 안 가던 기분이 들었는데 내가 예민한가 했거든
scenes.en: I kept feeling like the ball just wasn't going to him. I thought I was being paranoid.
say: Under a different report, another wrote:
I kept feeling like the ball just wasn't being passed to him. I thought I was being paranoid.

scenes.ko: 축구 대표팀 경기력이 개판인 이유가 있었네 저러니 조직력이 안 되지
scenes.en: So there WAS a reason the team played so badly. No wonder there was no teamwork.
say: And the top comment there connects it to results.
So there was a reason the team kept playing so badly. No wonder there was no teamwork.

scenes.title: Blaming the federation
say: Fourth. A lot of the anger was not aimed at the players at all.

scenes.ko: 윗물이 맑아야 아랫물도 맑은 법인데 협회가 썩었으니
scenes.en: The water downstream is only as clean as the water upstream. And the federation is rotten.
say: There's a Korean saying that the water downstream is only as clean as the water upstream.
Hundreds of viewers used it to blame the federation, which has faced years of criticism over how it runs the national team.

scenes.title: "No Sonny, no football"
say: Fifth. Something that might surprise viewers outside Korea.
For a lot of fans, Son is the reason they watch the national team at all.

scenes.ko: 손흥민 아니였음 국대 축구 관심도 없다... 정신 차려라
scenes.en: If it weren't for Son, I wouldn't even care about the national team. Get it together.
say: If it weren't for Son, I wouldn't even care about the national team. Get it together. That's over a thousand likes.

scenes.ko: 손흥민 은퇴하면 그깟 공놀이 안 보면 그만이다
scenes.en: When Son retires, I'll just stop watching. It's only a ball game.
say: And another: when Son retires, I'll just stop watching. It's only a ball game anyway.
Comments like these were everywhere. Shorter versions too. No Sonny, no football.

scenes.label: views on MBC's news recap of the retirement reports
say: That attachment is also why the numbers are so big.
An MBC news recap about the retirement reports alone has passed three point four million views.

scenes.title: The other side
say: But not everyone in Korea sees this as a simple story of a captain being bullied.

scenes.head: "Conflict exists in every team. The problem is that it went public."
say: Well-known commentator Park Moon-sung pointed out that conflict exists in every team, in every country.
In Europe, he said, these stories usually come out years later, in autobiographies. The real problem is that this one became public while the players are still playing together.
His suggestion: the people involved should say clearly where they stand, instead of letting rumors do the talking.

scenes.head: Some say a generational change is due — and that Son should consider giving up the armband
say: Other voices in Korean media argued that a generational change is overdue.
One club coach even suggested that Son should step down as captain and support the younger players.
And reports have also pointed to friction going back years, including an interview boycott during the World Cup.

scenes.title: What happens next
say: So what happens now?
Interim coach Roberto Moreno announces his November squad on October twenty-ninth.
Korea then plays Saudi Arabia on November thirteenth and Qatar on November seventeenth, both in Doha.
Korean media say the big question is simple. Does he call up both Son and the ninety-six line, and try to make it work?

items: A claim in parliament: teammates call Son "No. 7"
Others: conflict is normal, change is due
say: So, to sum up.
A claim in parliament that some players call their captain number seven.
A wave of sympathy, then anger.
Fans rewatching old matches and wondering what they missed.
Plenty of blame for the federation.
And a smaller group saying conflict is normal, and change is overdue.

scenes.ko: 손흥민선수 은퇴 얘기는 입에 담지도 마라. 이 상황에선 절대 안된다.
scenes.en: Don't even say the word "retire" about Son. Not now. Absolutely not.
say: And here is the comment I promised.
Don't even say the word retire about Son. Not now. Absolutely not.
That's what Korea is saying this week.
If you want to know what Koreans think about the next big story, subscribe. We'll translate it for you.
